notes.name: the fuel it holds in pounds, as the original's tanks are named (2700LB): a name with LB is a tank, its weight the fuel (stores.rs is_tank)
notes.model: the original's file name, which Models: Detailed draws as our 370 US gal tank (shared/extra/models/stores/f16ftk.glb, FlightGear's 370G.ac)
notes.kg: the fuel of a full tank: 370 US gal (1400.6 l) of JP-8 at 0.80 kg/l (inferred density), 1120 kg (2470 lb); the tank's own 443 lb (201 kg) empty is not counted, as the original counts a tank's weight as fuel only
notes.size: 18 1/4 ft (5.56 m) long, 26 1/2 in (0.673 m) across (f16net-tanks); our model's size is the original's 2700LB tank's (aircraft-models.md §5)
notes.drag: carriage drag index (10^4 x the drag coefficient on the F-16's 300 sq ft wing, flight-model.md §9.18): 0.15 x its 0.673 m across (f16net-tanks) frontal area, 0.15 the drag of a streamlined tank on its pylon on that area (inferred); the F-16 manual's published indices were not at hand
notes.motion: the reader's defaults (a jettisoned tank falls ballistic)

footnotes.f16net-tanks: F-16.net, "Luke F-16 jettisons fuel tanks, lands safely" (18 1/4 ft long, 26 1/2 in in diameter, 443 lb empty, 370 gallons), https://www.f-16.net/f-16-news-article2018.html
